    Fix use-after-free when XIncluding text from Reader

    before parsing has finished. Cache a copy of the text string, not the

message.content:
Now I understand the fix completely. The key change is:
1. `txtTab` stores `xmlChar*` (string copy) instead of `xmlNodePtr` (node pointer)
2. When loading from cache, it creates a new text node with `xmlNewText(ctxt->txtTab[i])` instead of `xmlCopyNode(ctxt->txtTab[i], 1)`

The UAF happens because:
1. First XInclude loads text, creates a text node, stores it in `txtTab[0]` and sets it as `incTab[0]->inc`
2. The text node is added to the document tree
3. The Reader frees the text node when it moves past it
4. Second XInclude references the same text URL, finds it in `txturlTab`, and tries `xmlCopyNode(ctxt->txtTab[0], 1)` - but `txtTab[0]` is a dangling pointer

My test didn't crash because the Reader might not be freeing the text node in this scenario. Let me check if the Reader actually frees the text node. Looking at the Reader code, it frees nodes when `reader->preserves == 0` and `reader->in_xinclude == 0`. 

The issue might be that the text node is added as a child of the XInclude element, and when the Reader processes the XInclude element, it might not free the text node immediately. Let me look at how `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` adds the text node to the document:
